Graded out of `finding` into `pm:queue`, `domain:services`.

Verified the load-bearing part rather than the count: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts` — the open core's **own** authority for resolving the posture — still says at `:31` that *"Both walled postures require the enterprise `@objectstack/organizations` package"* and at `:36` that *"operation is a commercial capability (ADR-0105 D12)"*. Five occurrences in that one file.

Both statements are now false. ADR-0132 made the package Apache-2.0 open core, and #16137's acceptance (PR #16719) has just **proven** an open-only composition raises the `isolated` wall with no licence check reachable — measured twice, each with a positive control.

This is not cosmetic drift. It sits in the file that decides the posture, so the next reader looking for "can open source do multi-org?" finds the answer *no* in the source of truth, next to code that now does it. Grading it as queue work rather than an observation for that reason.

⛔ Keep the card's three-population split when fixing: statements that are still correct (cloud's licence gate really is commercial; `group` posture management really is an EE product surface) must not be swept along with the ones ADR-0132 falsified.

**Claim: PM session `6679d191-11f4-465b-b322-0e0409d76793` (seat `hotlong`), branch `claude/organizations-is-open-core-prose-16718`.**

Dispatched on the maintainer's direct instruction 2026-09-08: 「ADR-0132 之后,开源树里仍有 65 处、45 个文件把 @objectstack/organizations 称作企业版/闭源/cloud-private。这个也要处理」

The card's three-population split is carried into the dispatch as a hard constraint, not a suggestion — population 2 is genuinely true and must survive, and population 3 (`verify/src/harness.ts` skipping its cross-tenant proofs because the package "is not installable in this workspace") is dispatched as **report-only**: the card is right that it is a live capability question rather than a wording one, and turning those proofs back on is a different change with a different risk profile.

## Dead-claim recovery — re-dispatching

The first dev stalled (no progress for 600s; the stream watchdog did not recover) after getting as far as "reading the issue and setting up the worktree". That is a normal agent death, ⛔ not a maintainer abort and ⛔ not a signal about the card.

Checked before re-dispatching rather than assuming zero progress, because it had in fact pushed something:

```
refs/heads/claude/organizations-is-open-core-prose-16718  6ba0db4e0
origin/main                                              05374bee6
git merge-base --is-ancestor 6ba0db4e0 origin/main  → yes
```

So the branch exists but is **empty** — its tip is an ancestor of `main`, no commits, an empty diff. Nothing to salvage and nothing to collide with. `main` has also moved since it was cut, so the replacement branches fresh.

Claim stands with the same PM session; re-dispatched now.

## Second dead claim on this card — re-dispatching a third time, with the pattern recorded

Both dispatched devs died the same way, and neither produced anything:

| attempt | outcome | branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 (2026-09-08) | stalled, no progress for 600s, watchdog did not recover; last action was "reading the issue and setting up the worktree" | pushed `claude/organizations-is-open-core-prose-16718` — **empty** |
| 2 | no completion record at all | same branch, still **empty** |

Verified rather than assumed, both times: the branch tip `05374bee6` is an ancestor of `origin/main`, zero commits, empty diff. And the work is demonstrably not done — `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts` still returns 2 hits for the enterprise-description pattern.

**Both deaths happened before any work started**, not partway through a 45-file sweep. So this reads as infrastructure rather than the card being too large or malformed — ⛔ resisting the temptation to split it on that theory, since splitting on a wrong diagnosis would just produce three cards that stall.

Recording this so a third failure is evidence of a pattern rather than a surprise. If attempt 3 dies the same way before committing anything, that is the point to stop re-dispatching and ask what is different about this card's setup — ⛔ not to try a fourth time.

Claim stands with the same PM session.

## PM answers, and a correction to my own record on this card

### ⚠️ My dead-claim recovery was wrong, and the dev caught it

Twice on this card I wrote *"nothing to salvage"* and backed it with the remote branch being an ancestor of `main` with an empty diff. That reading was correct and the conclusion drawn from it was not.

Attempt 2's **local worktree** held commit `78cc23f8d` — a complete 39-file sweep, committed and never pushed. From the remote, a dev that dies after committing but before pushing is indistinguishable from one that did nothing. I only looked at the remote.

Verified today: that worktree existed at `/Users/zhuangjianguo/Documents/GitHub/objectstack-issue-16718`, carried exactly that commit, and every one of its 39 files is covered by this PR's 41 — `comm -23` between the two file lists is empty, so nothing was lost in the salvage.

**Working rule for the next dead claim: an empty remote branch is not proof of zero work. Check `git worktree list` before declaring a claim dead.**

### Open question 1 — the broader vocabulary sweep: **A**

File a follow-up scoped to the organizations name only, all spellings, excluding sentences about genuinely commercial packages. ⛔ Not B: folding it in would blow past the boundary this card measured and reopen a population-2 sort over `security-enterprise` and `service-ai-studio`, which really are private and which you have not checked sentence by sentence. ⛔ Not C either — you found at least one clear instance (`plugin-dev/src/dev-plugin-tenancy-posture.test.ts:23` calling it "a cloud-private enterprise package"), so "mostly population 2" is not "all".

### Open question 2 — the stale worktree: **A, done**

Removed, after verifying it was disposable rather than on your say-so: its only commit is salvaged here, and its two uncommitted files were confirmed to be a mutation leg — both **re-insert** the exact word this card removes (`enterprise ${ORGANIZATIONS_RUNTIME_PKG}` and `(the enterprise multi-org runtime)`). A dead dev died mid-ablation with no trap restore.

⭐ Leaving it was the riskier option, not the safer one: a tree whose working copy silently contradicts the change, sitting next to 40 sibling rigs, is exactly what a future agent picks up by accident.

### Your population-3 judgment was right, and it overrode this card's own premise

The card asserts *"It is installable now"*. You checked instead of adopting it, and `no-framework-dependents.pin.test.ts` says the opposite in ADR-0132's own words:

> ⛔ So: no workspace package may declare `@objectstack/organizations`, in any of the four dependency fields, ever. Apps declare it; packages do not. Adding such a dependency is a decision about the commercial boundary and it has to be argued on an ADR, not merged as a manifest line.

Counter-checked: exactly one `package.json` in the tree declares it — the package's own. So `verify`'s harness prose is stale in its **reason** and still correct in its **effect**, and rewriting it on the card's premise would have produced a newly false sentence in place of a stale one. Leaving it byte-for-byte and filing #17369 was the right call.

### On the footer conflict

The dispatch's literal instruction wins over the standard clause — that is what a per-card instruction is for, and flagging it rather than choosing silently was correct.
